tumulto.p0: The anthology of the work of Wagner Barja (1985–2015), published on the occasion of the exhibition at Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil. Here the book becomes a site: each work has its space, all the texts that speak of it and the images in high resolution.
tumulto.p1: The Ministry of Culture and Banco do Brasil present Experiência Tumulto III, a panorama of the artistic production of Wagner Barja, an artist living in the federal capital. The exhibition reveals a “highly cohesive” body of work that, constituted over three decades, has always been marked by its experimental, irreverent and reflexive character, by its transit through diverse media and artistic languages, by the crossing of different domains, bodies of knowledge and sensibilities.
tumulto.p2: The exhibition comprises thirty works that make evident the diverse languages with which the artist works — visual poetry, videos and photographs, sculptures and installations, performances and urban interventions — and a previously unseen installation, “Jonas”.
tumulto.p3: Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, institutional text of the catalogue (2015).
tumulto.p4: “We see through enigmas, we hear through dissonances. It is this place outside place that Barja never ceases to open. That is why I suspect that this writing-art alongside is, above all, ‘artesemnome’.”
tumulto.p5: Marisa Flórido César, curator — opening text of the catalogue. Barja is a subverter of the codification of life and of art: he appropriates icons and myths, texts and objects, concepts and bodies of knowledge, and associates them in an improbable, at times laughable, way, unveiling the arbitrariness of signs and of discourses. João Batista meets another João, Beuys; the sun/eye of Goethe transforms itself into the fifth note of the scale; the eye converts itself into the eye-anus of Bataille.
tumulto.p6: All the records of the catalogue — from the Anthology of the work (1985–2015) to the video interventions and the installation Jonas. Each work gathers the texts that speak of it. No work was left out.
tumulto.p7: Video records of the interventions and performances of Wagner Barja: A Vitória do Gallo (Cachoeira do Arari, Ilha de Marajó — Funarte) and Despacho na Duna, a critique of the art circuit.
tumulto.p8: Jonas, the disobedient prophet, is swallowed by a whale on the high seas and remains there for three days, in a dark chamber. Barja, the riotous artist, returns the visitor to that belly: projected waters, open monads, word and image in suspension.
tumulto.p9: The following pages of the catalogue document the previously unseen multimedia installation created for Experiência Tumulto III, with a text by Maria Thereza Azevedo (“Jonas: deslocamentos e repetições em instalação multimídia”) and by Antônio Miranda (“Verbivocovisualidade na instalação Jonas”).

tumulto.p11: artistic production of Wagner Barja, an artist living in the federal capital. The exhibition reveals to us a “highly cohesive” body of work that, constituted over three decades, has always been marked by its experimental, irreverent and reflexive character, by its transit through diverse media and artistic languages, by the crossing of different domains, bodies of knowledge and sensibilities. The exhibition comprises thirty works that make evident the diverse languages with which the artist works – visual poetry, videos and photographs, sculptures and installations, performances and urban interventions – and a previously unseen installation, “Jonas”. In producing this anthology, Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil makes possible for the public the experimentation of contemporary art by means of new languages, contributes to education and to the democratization of culture, and values local artistic production. CENTRO CULTURAL BANCO DO BRASIL

In a world still to be seen, named, recreated, it is from silence that words are enunciated, it is from the invisible that the image glimmers, facing both incompleteness and the blind saturation of visibilities and the tyranny of discourses. We stumble in the vertigo of the word, in the blindness of images. Not by chance, both questions important to Wagner Barja. Experiência Tumulto III - divided in two sessions, “Anthology” and the previously unseen installation “Jonas” - gathers his production realized over three decades and which has always transited through diverse media and artistic expressions, through distinct domains, crossing and interrogating bodies of knowledge and sensibilities. We are introduced into a universe that overflows in “animaverbovocovisual” poems (his “worknames”), installations and interventions, performances or videos. A profusion of images, objects and words, texts and characters that intertwine, as if they founded or stirred a world in continuous process of transmutation. A fabulous cosmogony in which bizarre creatures wander, hybrids
tumulto.p13: Jonas, the disobedient prophet, is swallowed by a whale on the high seas and remains there for three days, in the ship's hold. Barja, the riotous artist, vomits the vertebrae of the whale, but before that, he digs into the bone to inject/nest images, pouring and inverting memories of waters into that which gives support to the bodies. Victor Turner affirms that every experience is a risk and a trans-form. In the work Jonas, of Wagner Barja, the experience/risk is that of an invisible performer who practices the idea of body without organs of Antonin Artaud. tumulto.p14: deep, shallow, murky, tranquil, violent, red. Water, generator of life and of crossing, never ceases to dissolve and to transform itself. Bachelard recalls that the dreamer of water is a being in vertigo who constantly lets something of himself collapse. For him water is matter that is always about to become another. The hybrids and the out of place provoke estrangements, as provoked the mythical monsters of the Middle Ages or the ready-mades of Marcel Duchamp. They riot, dis-arrange, de-stabilize and lead to rearrangements in our perception. Synthesis work of the exhibition Experiência Tumulto III, Jonas carries the trajectory of the artist, who has been practicing displacements since Deitado eternamente of 1986. It is a taking of things out of place and a reordering, but not without first passing through the entrails of the anthropophagic tumult, which can instigate territories of existence and alter hegemonic modes of subjectivation. In the witches' cauldron of contemporary art, potions are stirred that mix procedures brought from art history. Richards) intends to translate the semiotic relation made explicit by Charles Sanders Peirce as imperative in the understanding of signific-ation. It is not the case here to present all the unfoldings of this interpretant—object—sign relation, only to stress that the interpretant acts from its own experience, memory, worldview, interpretive capacity, ontological or sensory, depending on the anima that animates this “gaze”. In the case of “Jonas” here referenced, besides the texts of presentation of the work, there exists the possible (“vocal”, subjective) evocation of the biblical character swallowed by the whale, who inspired the work of the artist. The “whale” is represented objectually by means of hanging “vertebrae”, not in sequence, but as an exhibition set, containing electronic devices showing images of marine waves (luminous), forming an impressive and impactful, yet poetic, ensemble.
